content.text:
Confirmed: `getClassSuffix()` returns `clazz.getClassSuffix()`, which can be `null` (as evidenced by the `c.getClassSuffix() == null` null-check used a few lines above in the same method). So this can legitimately return null, and the loop added in commit `1f1b51617` calls `section.setName(course.getUniqueId(), c.getClassSuffix(course))` without guarding against that null value, which is exactly what the fix commit addresses.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 1f1b516171664d26669bc59009aefd81aaa76a17

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the fixed method's full history with `git log -p --follow -- StudentSectioningDatabaseLoader.java` and searched for when the exact faulty line `section.setName(course.getUniqueId(), c.getClassSuffix(course));` was introduced (as opposed to merely being modified). This search found a single earlier commit that added that line verbatim (within a newly-added `for` loop), with no change to it in between that point and the bug-fixing commit.

(2) Commit `1f1b51617` (2017-06-20, "tomas-muller") added:
```java
for (CourseOffering course: io.getCourseOfferings())
    section.setName(course.getUniqueId(), c.getClassSuffix(course));
```
This passes the result of `c.getClassSuffix(course)` directly to `section.setName(...)` without checking for `null`. The bug-fixing commit (`df2beb076`) simply inserts a null check (`if (suffix != null) section.setName(...)`), confirming the original omission is what was defective.

(3) Supporting evidence: In `Class_.getClassSuffix(CourseOffering)` (`JavaSource/org/unitime/timetable/model/Class_.java:1672`), the suffix is delegated to `getExternalClassNameHelper().getClassSuffix(this, courseOffering)`, and the default implementation (`DefaultExternalClassNameHelper.getClassSuffix`) simply returns `clazz.getClassSuffix()` — the same field that is explicitly null-checked a few lines above in the loader (`c.getClassSuffix() == null ? ... : c.getClassSuffix()`), proving this value is routinely null in practice. Thus storing a null name via `section.setName` was a real, reachable defect introduced exactly in this commit, with no intervening modification of that line before the fix.

I'm highly confident in this attribution, since the exact faulty code was introduced wholesale in one commit and remained unchanged until the fix.
